name: Second Shift Skills Library
about: A free, open library of agent skills hosted by Second Shift. No account, no paywall. Each entry states its class and its what-it-can-touch line. A skill teaches an agent how to do something; it never grants permission to do it. Check the license field on each entry before redistributing.

guide.note: Fetch this skill first; it teaches the library’s own conventions.

skills.name: Find Second Shift Skills
skills.description: The library’s own guide skill, written by Second Shift. It teaches an agent to read the public index (one JSON document), choose a skill by its description, class, and what-it-touches line, and fetch the raw SKILL.md from its stable URL — no account, no sign-in. It also states the library’s ground rule: a skill teaches an agent how to do something; it never grants permission to do it.
skills.capability: Teaches any agent to use this library: read the index, pick the skill that fits the job, and fetch its SKILL.md.
skills.touches: Reads this library’s index; touches nothing of yours.
skills.review: First-party: written and maintained by Second Shift.

skills.name: Agent Reach
skills.description: Read-only reach across the platforms agents are usually blind to: X/Twitter, Reddit, YouTube (subtitles and transcripts), GitHub, LinkedIn and job boards, Instagram, Facebook, RSS feeds, podcasts, and general web search. Reach for it when a job starts with a link, a platform, or a question the open web can answer. It reads and reports; it never posts, comments, or logs in as anyone.
skills.capability: Lets an agent read the live internet: search and pull posts, comments, transcripts, and pages from X, Reddit, YouTube, GitHub, LinkedIn, RSS, and the open web.
skills.touches: Reads public web content only. Never posts, comments, likes, or logs in as you.
skills.review: Reviewed: read in full and installed by the Second Shift fleet on 2026-11-06. The file served here is that reviewed copy.
skills.caveat: What you get here is the skill file itself. Several of its channels connect through a companion command-line tool, and the channels that read through your own browser logins (X, Reddit, Instagram) are a separate opt-in. They are not part of this download and nothing here enables them.
